status: resolved in this wave; the trap is durable and applies to every EditMode fixture that checks wire types
authority: NUnit XML under editmode-full/ and collision-payload-redgreen/ at HEAD; read on 2026-08-11
conclusion: A JSON *type* assertion must be made against the raw serialized envelope string. Asserting against a SimpleJSON node's ToString() measures the parser, not the wire, and this build of SimpleJSON re-quotes every scalar.

what_happened.1: A code review asked the fixture to reject a string-typed relative_speed, because the frozen contract's collision branch declares {"relative_speed": {"type": "number"}} and the previous assertion used AsFloat, which coerces "3.5" and would have passed a contract-violating payload.
what_happened.2: The remediation matched a JSON-number regex against collision["payload"].ToString().
what_happened.3: That turned the fixture RED: 'relative_speed is absent, non-finite, or not serialized as a JSON number: {"contact_ids":[ "contact:2:10:0:10|20:0:20:0", "contact:2:10:0:10|20:0:20:1" ], "relative_speed":"3.5"}'.
what_happened.4: The product was never wrong. PhysicsCaptureProtocol.cs:225 writes the value through AppendFloat, which appends value.ToString("R", InvariantCulture) unquoted (line 245-248). The quotes and the interior spaces in the failure message are SimpleJSON's own re-serialization, not the bytes the envelope carries.

mechanism: This SimpleJSON build stores every scalar as text and re-quotes it on ToString, so a parsed node cannot distinguish a JSON number from a JSON string. Any assertion made after JSONNode.Parse has already lost the type distinction it is trying to check.
why_it_matters_beyond_this_fixture: The false direction runs both ways. Before the remediation the fixture used AsFloat and was GREEN — it would have stayed GREEN against a genuinely string-typed wire value, which the Python consumer rejects. After the naive remediation it was RED against correct output. Neither state carried information about the wire.

the_fix.assertion: Regex.Matches(eventsJson, "\"contact_ids\":\\[[^\\]]*\\],\"relative_speed\":(-?[0-9][0-9.eE+-]*)") must have exactly one match, and its group must parse to the recorded magnitude
the_fix.why_this_shape: eventsJson is the string returned by EnvelopeJson(envelope, true) — the bytes the envelope carries. The pattern anchors on contact_ids, which only the collision branch of the frozen oneOf carries, so it stays scoped to a collision payload instead of any event that happens to serialize a speed. The count assertion keeps it pinned to this fixture's single collision. A leading -?[0-9] rejects NaN and Infinity, which AppendFloat's "R" format writes as bare words.

verification.red_green: collision-payload-redgreen.json — RED against the mutated emitter (fixture Failed, 13/14), source restored to 0987580887fb07603d1b4174effbdfc83c6cfef8b8554d4d8eaed7934cc879d6 byte-identically, GREEN at HEAD (fixture Passed, 14/14)

verification.authority: NUnit XML result attributes. Every EditMode invocation on this host exits -6 from a signal inside CEF shutdown, reached after the run finished and after the XML was written; the exit code is not authoritative.

durable_rule: In this project's EditMode fixtures, assert JSON structure through SimpleJSON and JSON scalar types through the raw serialized string. Never mix the two.
